items.question: What great accomplishment makes one dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation are valued attainments
A great accomplishment combines enjoyment and liberation
Such accomplishment can inspire favor
items.inference: One who attains the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: One may become dear to the yoginīs through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter concludes after emerging in the moon island?
premises: A textual section is identified by number
The section is located in the moon island context
The section has emerged or concluded there
items.inference: The ninth chapter, emerged in the moon island, is concluded.
uncertainties: The exact sense of vinirgate as emerged or issued is contextual.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self surrounded by fire?
premises: The self is the object of visualization
Fire surrounds the visualized self
The posture is standing on one foot
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What request is made to the god regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: Knowledge requires determination
The speaker addresses the god
The speaker asks for manifestation now
items.inference: The speaker asks the god to make the determination of knowledge manifest today.
items.plain_english: O God, make the determination of knowledge manifest to me today.

items.question: What division of the eight octads is sought to be known fully?
premises: There is a division of eight octads
This division is an object of inquiry
Complete knowledge of it is desired
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.
uncertainties: The adverb anantathā may qualify the extent or manner of knowing.
items.plain_english: And to know fully, without end, the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How is accomplishment quickly attained in the secret place as a wheel?
premises: A secret place is identified as a wheel
Accomplishment occurs in that context
The accomplishment happens quickly
items.inference: O Bhairava, accomplishment is quickly attained in the secret place understood as a wheel.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation between sthānaṃ and cakraṃ is compact.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how accomplishment comes quickly in the secret place as a wheel.

items.question: Why does Bhairava praise the great goddess for her difficult question?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval
The great goddess has asked a question
The matter asked about is hard for gods to obtain
items.inference: Bhairava praises the great goddess because she has asked about something difficult even for the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O Great Goddess! I have been asked about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable kṣa is assigned a specific locus
The syllable laṃ is assigned another locus
These loci are named as brahmarandhra and forehead
items.inference: The syllable kṣa is in the state of the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region.
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is at the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa placed within the body?
premises: The syllable ṣa is assigned to a bodily region
The syllable śa is assigned to another bodily region
The throat region and heart are specified
items.inference: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

items.question: What follows after the place-wheels have been declared to the beloved?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
These wheels have an associated meditation
The beloved is invited to listen
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation for the beloved to hear.
items.plain_english: The place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: What form does the first meditative lotus take in this practice?
premises: A lotus is the object of meditation
The lotus has eight spokes
The lotus is adorned by the first octad
items.inference: The first meditative form is a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: Meditate on a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with equanimous mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equanimous mind
Certain social conduct is contrasted with this state
Abandonment is prescribed
items.inference: Through practice, one with an equanimous mind should abandon village dharma.
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ likely refers to conventional worldly duties.
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an equanimous mind, one should abandon the ways of ordinary village life.

items.question: What powers arise from this practice according to the teaching to the beloved?
premises: The practice yields special knowledge
Hearing at a distance is one attainment
Paralysis of bonds is another attainment
items.inference: The practice grants knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the paralysis of bonds, O beloved.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham may mean arresting or stunning bonds or fetters.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains the knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are summarized briefly for the goddess?
premises: Additional results are being listed
Immortality is one such result
Transformation is another result stated briefly
items.inference: In brief, the attainments include immortality and likewise transformation, O goddess.
uncertainties: The specific nature of parivartanam is not detailed here.
items.plain_english: O goddess, in brief, one also attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second meditative lotus characterized in this teaching?
premises: A second lotus is introduced
It has eight petals
It is brightly illuminated by fire meditation
items.inference: The second lotus is eight-petaled and well illuminated by meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, brilliantly illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in single-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes one-pointed in meditation
Such focus produces a special capacity
The capacity involves creating forms
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in single-pointed meditation can create forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power does the practitioner possess when angered?
premises: The practitioner can become angry
Anger activates a destructive capacity
The scope includes the entire triple world
items.inference: When angry, the practitioner can destroy the entire triple world with all its moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced
Wheels have specific functions
This wheel relates to nine principles
items.inference: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.
uncertainties: The exact set of nine tattvas is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel's practice?
premises: The practice affects bodily aging signs
The practice affects perception
Wrinkles, grey hair, and distant seeing are mentioned
items.inference: The practice brings destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise seeing from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

rows.grounds: object of intent; sandhi form of dhyānam

items.question: What disciplined practice in solitude enables the creation of many forms?
premises: Solitude is the setting for practice
Meditation requires focused intent
Multiple forms can be produced
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, one should create forms in many ways.
uncertainties: dhyānañ shows sandhi before ca; analyzed as accusative object.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What result comes to one devoted to constant practice?
premises: Constant practice is required
The practitioner is devoted to that practice
Immortality is presented as a result
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is devoted to constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from eating by day affect death from aging?
premises: A regimen of non-eating by day is specified
Death associated with age is the concern
The practice leads to overcoming that death
items.inference: By not eating during the day, one will go beyond death from aging.
uncertainties: The compound vayo-mṛtyuṃ is interpreted as death due to age.
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death from aging.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: Constant yogic practice is maintained
A specific duration is indicated
The practitioner’s form changes accordingly
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one’s form becomes like that of a sixteen-year-old.
uncertainties: dvi-aṣṭa-varṣa-ākṛtiḥ is interpreted as the form of sixteen years.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What contemplative visualization grants the power to shake the triple world?
premises: A specific color is to be contemplated
The contemplation is performed always
The result is power over the triple world
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world, O beloved.
uncertainties: The object that is smoke-colored is implicit in the verse.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
